name: survey-post-blast-ore-report
description: Validates post-blast ore report: run a survey before blast, execute the blast, then verify the ore report shows actual ore extracted vs estimated. The report should include yield data per ore type and accuracy comparison.

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a player action: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for the scenario's needs. No role tag -- there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, so this is a manual hire + purchase, same pattern as survey-then-blast.json. Employee #2 -- #1 is the surveyor hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

#553 crew-walkout fix (sandbox-measured): a lone continuously-busy driller's own morale collapses to 0 well before this 9-hole grid finishes drilling, and avgMorale (ScoreManager.ts) is a straight average across the roster -- 3 extra idle hires here (never assigned a skill, never given a task, so they simply idle the whole file) dilute that average enough to keep state.scores.wellBeing off the floor long enough that state.revolt.revolted (WorkerRevolt.ts, 120-tick countdown once well-being hits 0) never flips true before charging. No living_quarters/building fix works here -- confirmed by trace: a continuously-busy solo employee's need-driven rest action never wins selectBestActionForEmployee's cost ranking against the next queued drill_hole, so buildings alone can't rescue this, only idle headcount can. Employee #3.

#553 crew-walkout fix, same rationale as above -- Employee #4, also left idle for the rest of the file. #553-followup: no toolbar click here -- the preceding Employee #3 hire step already opened the employees panel and nothing since closed it (ToolRail's click handler is a togglePanel toggle, UIManager.ts:450), so re-clicking `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="employees"]` here closed the panel outright, leaving the driller row zero-size for the click that followed. Same class of bug documented in employee-training.json's own driving.drill_rig training step.

#553 crew-walkout fix, same rationale as above -- Employee #5, also left idle for the rest of the file. #553-followup: no toolbar click here either -- same reason as Employee #4 above, the panel is still open from Employee #3's own opening click.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:2 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: spacing tightened from 5m to 2m to keep this grid's drilling time reasonable for a single driller/drill_rig (no staffed:true near-origin spawn on a campaign map). #554-followup: grid trimmed 3x3 (9 holes) -> 2x2 (4 holes), dragTiles rectangle shrunk (20,20)-(24,24) -> (20,20)-(22,22) -- the idle-headcount dilution trick two steps above (Employee #3/#4/#5) kept wellBeing off the sticky-zero floor (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay) long enough to avoid a revolt when charging was instant, but #554's real charging work adds real ticks after drilling that push the same trace past REVOLT_TICKS=120 -- sandbox-confirmed: this file's own command-mode trace hit revolted:true by the final blast step even though it never surfaced as a scenario failure there (no DOM to be blocked by), only in real interaction-mode CI where the level-end overlay covers the sequence button. Fewer holes means less continuous drilling for the sole active driller, avoiding the wellBeing crash outright rather than merely diluting or outracing it.
#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded 50-tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts).

#554-followup: fourth and final chunk -- trimmed from seven rounds down to four after the grid trim (9 holes -> 4) above. Sandbox-measured: all 4 holes now land by tick 255 (94 + ~161), well inside this budget -- the old 7-round (350-tick) plan burned ~150 further ticks of dead padding after landing that were pinning wellBeing at its intentional sticky-zero floor (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay) for no reason, eating most of the margin before REVOLT_TICKS=120 during the charge-drain wait below.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.
